construct: Autonomous aldosterone excess increases epithelial sodium-channel activity and basolateral Na+-K+ ATPase activity in collecting-duct principal cells, increasing sodium reabsorption and creating conditions that enhance renal potassium secretion; volume expansion suppresses renin and hydrogen-ion loss contributes to metabolic alkalosis.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: High aldosterone with suppressed renin, resistant hypertension, hypokalemia, and alkalosis identifies primary aldosteronism; principal-cell ENaC/Na-K ATPase activation drives potassium secretion.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Reduced ENaC or Na-K ATPase activity would oppose potassium wasting. NKCC2 and NCC loss cause secondary salt-wasting syndromes, not the direct principal-cell response to autonomous aldosterone.
